headline: Revenue climbs modestly while margins and profit shrink
summary_short: Revenue rose 5.4% y/y to $1.10B, but GAAP operating margin fell to 7% and diluted EPS dropped 26.8% y/y to $0.52 as stock-based comp and CIS infrastructure investment ramped.
summary_long: Revenue rose 5.4% y/y to $1.10B, led by Cloud Infrastructure Services (+39% y/y to $99M) and Security (+10% y/y to $604M); Delivery and other cloud applications fell 6% y/y to $396M. GAAP operating margin compressed to 7% (non-GAAP 25%) as stock-based compensation rose to $146.3M from $112.8M y/y and capex jumped to $346.5M (32% of revenue) on CIS infrastructure buildout. Diluted EPS fell 26.8% y/y to $0.52 (non-GAAP $1.59, down 8% y/y). Cash and marketable securities rose to $4.62B after a $3.45B convertible-notes issuance; the company repurchased $410M of stock. Q3 guidance: revenue $1,105-1,130M, non-GAAP EPS $1.60-1.80.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited sustained momentum in security and Cloud Infrastructure Services, highlighting year-to-date CIS contracts worth over $2.8B, including a new $600M+ four-year deal for AI/robotics infrastructure.
Growth driven by Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue up 39% y/y to $99M and Security revenue up 10% y/y to $604M, partially offset by a 6% y/y decline in Delivery and other cloud applications.
Cost growth outpaced the 5.4% revenue gain: stock-based compensation rose to $146.3M from $112.8M y/y and total costs grew faster than revenue, compressing GAAP operating margin from 15% to 7%.
Lower operating income combined with 5.8% y/y growth in diluted share count drove diluted EPS down more than the net-income decline alone would imply.
Cash rose mainly from a $3.45B convertible senior notes issuance in the quarter, per the financing-activities section of the cash flow statement, partially offset by $410M of share repurchases.
